parts.problem_md:
When a person changes their password they are asked to verify that it has been entered correctly by re-entering the password.

**State **what this type of verification is called.
parts.solution_md:
This type of verification is called:

- Double (data) entry **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
A new patient is attending a medical centre. He completes a form with his details and gives this to the secretary who enters the details into a database.

The secretary carefully checks the details entered into the database with those on the form.

**State **what this process is called.
parts.solution_md:
This process is called:

- Visual verification **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
A librarian in a college department library is entering data into a student borrowers’ file. As the data is entered it needs to be verified.

**Describe **the **two **types of verification.
parts.solution_md:
The two types of verification are:

**Visual verification ****[1 mark]**

- Person enters the data it is read through and corrected as needed using the original copy **[1 mark]**

**Double data entry ****[1 mark]**

- Person types the data then retypes the data from the original copy/source **[1 mark]**
- Person types the data and another types the data from the original copy/source **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **One mark** for correct verification type and max **one mark** for description

parts.problem_md: **Explain**, using examples, why it is necessary to carry out validation as well as verification for this system.
parts.solution_md:
It is important to carry out validation as well as verification due to:

Max **three **of the following:

- Not all errors are found by validation and verification separately **[1 mark]**
- Source document may contain errors **[1 mark]**
- Verification only checks that data is copied correctly **[1 mark]**
- Verification does not check if data is reasonable/sensible **[1 mark]**
- Validation checks are carried out automatically by the computer **[1 mark]**

Max **two **from the following:

- Correct appropriate example of a verification check e.g. data supplied by the borrower is incorrect on the source document and was copied **[1 mark]**
- Correct appropriate explanation of an example of a validation check e.g. (Number of books borrowed is 1 misread as a 7; in a range check of 1 –10) **[1 mark]**

The table shows examples of the stock.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medihoney | 3081043612211 | 15 | Capimed | 0126 |
| Sodium fusidate | 1437210227870 | 60 | Brooks Medical | 0112 |
| Crepe bandage | 2541233164353 | 100 | Capimed | 0064 |
| Crepe bandage | 2834954736849 | 89 | Cams Meds | 0064 |

As data is entered it needs to be verified and validated.

**Explain **why verification is carried out
parts.solution_md:
Verification checks are carried out as it:

parts.problem_md:
RockIT Airlines representatives use a computer booking system to book flights for customers.

A representative from the airline types in the customer reference number, the number of passengers, departure time, departure date, departure airport and the destination airport.

A customer is planning to take a flight from London Heathrow Airport. The representative types in a code LHR for London Heathrow Airport. One of the reasons for using a code for the airport is to improve data accuracy.

**Describe **the importance of data accuracy when making a booking.
parts.solution_md:
The importance of accuracy is can be described as:

Any** two **of the following:

- If the data is typed in incorrectly then the booking may be rejected **[1 mark]**
- If an incorrect airport code is used they may fly to the wrong airport **OR **May miss the flight **[1 mark]**
- If the customer reference number is typed in incorrectly then the booking may be assigned to the wrong person **[1 mark]**
- If the number of passengers is incorrectly entered then number of seats will be wrong/overbooked **[1 mark]**
- So that the wrong booking is not made **[1 mark]**

The student checks the text he has written using a spell checker.

**Explain **how a spell checker works
parts.solution_md:
A spell check works by:

Any **two **of the following:

- Compares each typed word… **[1 mark]**
- …with its dictionary/database **[1 mark]**
- Uses algorithms to check the spelling **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md: **Explain **why the suggestions made by the spell checker do not always give the correct response.
parts.solution_md:
The suggestions made by the spell checker do not always give the correct response as:

Any **two **of the following:

- Real names are not recognised **[1 mark]**
- Badly spelt words will not be recognised **[1 mark]**
- Incorrect grammar may not be recognised **[1 mark]**
- It will not find words that sound the same but have been used incorrectly **[1 mark]**
- Some words may be spelt incorrectly but form another word **[1 mark]**
- They do not learn from their mistakes unless added to the dictionary **[1 mark]**
- They may use the wrong dictionary **[1 mark]**
